business_problem: Biofy needed to shorten infectious-disease diagnosis from days to hours and improve antibiotic recommendations, but genome assembly, vector search, and model training were too compute-intensive for CPUs and traditional hospital workflows to support in clinically useful timeframes.
solution_summary: Biofy built a cloud-native diagnostic pipeline on NVIDIA-accelerated infrastructure to turn full-genome sequencing into treatment recommendations. The platform assembles bacterial genomes, embeds them as vectors, and compares those vectors against a larger genomic and resistance database to identify pathogens and probable resistance profiles. Biofy's Abby recommendation engine then evaluates the detected genes and suggests the best antibiotics or treatment options so results can feed directly into hospital workflows. Training and serving run on OCI AI infrastructure with NVIDIA GPUs and H100 Tensor Core GPUs, which let the company process high-throughput genomic workloads fast enough for practical clinical turnaround. By combining sequencing, vector search, and AI recommendations in one accelerated stack, Biofy shifted diagnosis from a multiday manual-lab process to a rapid, data-driven workflow that improves both speed and confidence for clinicians.

data_flow: DNA sequencing output is assembled into genomes, embedded and matched against microbial and resistance databases on NVIDIA-backed infrastructure, and then passed into Abby so clinicians receive pathogen identification and antibiotic recommendations directly in the care workflow.
business_outcome: Biofy cut end-to-end time to treatment recommendation from five days to four hours, raised diagnostic accuracy to 95–97%, improved infrastructure performance by 50% at up to half the cost of alternatives, and made same-day personalized antibiotic guidance feasible for hospitals.
